Position Summary...

What you'll do...

Fulfillment Experience builds the capabilities and operating mechanisms that make Walmart a reliable, convenient on-demand partner. Our teams determine what customers can buy, the promise and fulfillment choices they see, how orders are managed and recovered, and how the network performs at scale. We partner across Product, Engineering, Data Science, Finance, Merchandising, Store Operations, Fulfillment Centers, Last Mile, Transportation, and Strategy to improve customer outcomes while balancing speed, assortment, cost, and operational feasibility.

Role summary

The (USA) Manager, Technology Operations identifies and solves complex, high-impact fulfillment problems across a defined product, operational, or customer-experience area. This role turns ambiguous customer, operational, and financial signals into a clear diagnosis, an aligned plan, and measurable results. Working across Product, Engineering, Data Science, Finance, and operations partners, the Manager leads initiatives from discovery and analysis through decision, delivery, readiness, and impact measurement. Success requires structured problem solving, clear communication, sound business judgment, and the ability to influence without direct authority.

What you'll do

• Own a complex problem space or initiative that improves customer experience, fulfillment performance, or financial outcomes.

• Use customer, operational, and financial data to identify opportunities, quantify impact, isolate root causes, and define success measures.

• Translate ambiguous problems into clear problem statements, hypotheses, options, and data-driven recommendations.

• Lead cross-functional solution design and execution with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Finance, Store Operations, Fulfillment Centers, Last Mile, Transportation, and other partners.

• Build and manage end-to-end plans that make ownership, milestones, dependencies, risks, decision points, pilots, launch readiness, and success measures clear.

• Drive alignment and resolve trade-offs without direct authority; escalate issues with a clear recommendation when timely leadership decisions are needed.

• Create concise, executive-ready updates and decision materials that clarify what changed, why it matters, and the action required.

• Measure results after launch, identify gaps or unintended outcomes, and drive refinements, scaling, or corrective action.

• Improve the team's planning, visibility, and execution through better processes, tools, automation, and operating routines.

What you'll bring

• Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives in eCommerce, supply chain, operations, product, strategy, analytics, or another fast-paced, data-rich environment.

• Strong structured problem-solving skills, including the ability to turn ambiguous issues into clear questions, synthesize disparate inputs, identify root causes, and recommend a practical path forward.

• Strong analytical fluency and comfort using data to form hypotheses, assess trade-offs, define metrics, and measure impact.

• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to make complex work understandable and action-oriented for audiences at every level.

• Proven ability to influence without authority, build trust across functions, navigate competing priorities, and drive commitments to closure.

• Disciplined program-management skills, including planning, milestone management, dependency and risk management, and launch or change readiness.

• Sound customer, operational, and financial judgment; able to balance the ideal solution with what is practical to execute at scale.

• A high-ownership mindset, curiosity, attention to detail, and a bias for action.

• Experience partnering directly with Product, Engineering, and Data Science teams to deliver technology-enabled business outcomes.

• Experience in omnichannel retail, eCommerce, fulfillment, supply chain, marketplaces, or a similarly complex operating environment.

• Working knowledge of SQL, BI and visualization tools, Jira, Airtable, or process-automation tools.

jobs.description:
Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 122,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.

JOB DESCRIPTION:

About Abbott

Abbott is a global healthcare leader, creating breakthrough science to improve people’s health. We’re always looking towards the future, anticipating changes in medical science and technology.

Working at Abbott

At Abbott, you can do work that matters, grow, and learn, care for yourself and your family, be your true self, and live a full life. You’ll also have access to:

• Career development with an international company where you can grow the career you dream of.
• Employees can qualify for free medical coverage in our Health Investment Plan (HIP) PPO medical plan in the next calendar year.
• An excellent retirement savings plan with a high employer contribution
• Tuition reimbursement, the Freedom 2 Save student debt program, and FreeU education benefit - an affordable and convenient path to getting a bachelor’s degree.
• A company recognized as a great place to work in dozens of countries worldwide and named one of the most admired companies in the world by Fortune.
• A company that is recognized as one of the best big companies to work for as well as the best place to work for diversity, working mothers, female executives, and scientists.

The Opportunity

Our Abbott story is one of delivering bold solutions in the face of complex healthcare challenges. At Abbott Electrophysiology (EP), we’ve been a leader for over 20 years, pioneering one of the first mapping systems, introducing the first contact force ablation catheter and creating a portfolio of products trusted in millions of procedures around the world. We have and will continue to redefine what’s possible in an evolving and challenging EP landscape.

When you join Abbott EP, you become part of a passionate group of individuals who are dedicated to driving the EP space forward and helping people live longer, fuller lives. We are committed to building a foundation for our people to be successful, investing in their development and growth, and creating a diverse, inclusive culture that welcomes different perspectives, experiences and backgrounds.

What You’ll Work On

Working under general direction, provides engineering, sales, educational and technical support in response to field inquiries from physicians, health care professionals, patients, and field sales staff, involving EP products.  Performs work that involves a high degree of independence. Identifies and routinely uses the most effective, cost efficient and best business practices to execute processes; continually evaluates their effectiveness and appropriateness. Exercises independent judgment in planning, organizing and performing work; monitors performance and reports status to manager.

As a Clinical Associate on the U.S. Abbott EP team, you will provide clinical and technical support in a hospital setting, utilizing EP technology in the treatment of various cardiac arrhythmias. You will join a high-functioning, collaborative team, partnering closely with  physicians and hospital staff to support the diagnosis and treatment of abnormal heart rhythms to achieve better patient outcomes. In this role, individuals will exercise independent judgment in planning, organizing, and performing day-to-day tasks. You will identify and routinely use the most effective, cost-efficient, and best business practices to execute processes, regularly communicating insights, feedback, and results to managers and team. Additional responsibilities include:

• Gaining foundational knowledge of EP through a structured training program with a strong emphasis on hands-on learning and practical application.

• Providing regional EP procedural case coverage in an Electrophysiology lab and/or operating room setting.

• Acting as a clinical interface between the medical community and the business.

• Demonstrating the ability to build and sustain credible clinical relationships with customers and sharing product expertise accordingly.

• Demonstrating a thorough command of all EP products, including technical details, software utilization, and capabilities.

• Providing engineering, sales, education, and clinical support on the safe and effective use of Abbott EP products, including cardiac mapping, diagnostic, and therapy systems.

• Supporting EP Sales Representatives in the following areas: Collaborating with sales personnel; Facilitating regional training seminars; Participating in clinical studies/data collection; Troubleshooting; and, Leading/supporting new product in-service trainings and/or demonstrations to physicians, nurses, and sales representatives. Continuously develops engineering, sales and technical skills aligned with the overall territory strategy, including learning from senior sales personnel and management.

• Staying up-to-date on the latest industry developments, regulatory requirements, and maintains strong knowledge of company and competitor products, market trends, and strategic goals.

• Providing management with feedback on market trends and customer insights to inform strategic decisions and guide next-generation product development.

• Participating in occasional travel for in-person instruction and live procedure coverage.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelors Degree or equivalent experience.
• Verification that you will satisfy all vendor credentialing requirements, which may include vaccination for COVID-19. If you require a medical or religious accommodation from these requirements or if you would like to understand more about these requirements, please advise HR so that we can provide additional information and if needed, we can explore any needed accommodation(s).

Apply Now

Learn more about our health and wellness benefits, which provide the security to help you and your family live full lives:  www.abbottbenefits.com

Follow your career aspirations to Abbott for diverse opportunities with a company that can help you build your future and live your best life. Abbott is an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to employee diversity.

Connect with us at www.abbott.com, on Facebook at www.facebook.com/Abbott, and on Twitter @AbbottNews.

jobs.description:
About AstraZeneca:

At AstraZeneca, we pride ourselves on crafting a collaborative culture that champions knowledge-sharing, ambitious thinking and innovation—ultimately providing employees with the opportunity to work across teams, functions and even the globe.

Recognizing the importance of individualized flexibility, our ways of working allow employees to balance personal and work commitments while ensuring we continue to create a strong culture of collaboration and teamwork through face-to-face engagement in our offices three days a week. Our head office and BlueSky Hub in downtown Toronto are purposefully designed with collaboration in mind, providing spaces where teams can come together to strategize, brainstorm and connect on key projects.

Our dedication to sustainability is also central to our culture and part of what makes AstraZeneca a great place to work. We know that the health of people, the planet and our business are interconnected, which is why we are taking ambitious action to tackle some of the biggest challenges of our time—from climate change to access to healthcare and disease prevention.

Role Summary:

The Director is accountable for setting the insights, analytics and AI-enabled evidence agenda for a key brand. As a member of the Brand Leadership Team, this role influences senior commercial, medical and market access decisions by translating data, market signals, customer needs and digital opportunities into clear strategic choices, measurable outcomes and enterprise value.

Role Overview:

The Director acts as a strategic partner to senior leaders, integrating market, customer, scientific, real-world, competitive and digital signals to shape brand strategy, customer engagement, launch excellence and growth.

This role also sets expectations for the responsible use of data, digital tools and artificial intelligence, ensuring that outputs are trusted, compliant, inclusive, explainable and linked to business value, patient impact and enterprise priorities.

Key Responsibilities:

Insights Generation and AI-Enabled Decision Support

• Set the strategic insights agenda for the brand, aligned with enterprise strategy, brand ambition, launch turning points, investment decisions and measurable outcomes.
• Integrate primary market research, competitive intelligence, secondary data, real-world data, digital engagement signals, advanced analytics and AI-enabled tools to inform brand strategy, forecasting, resource allocation and investment decisions.
• Translate complex data and external signals into clear recommendations, helping senior leaders understand opportunities, trade-offs, risks and execution implications.
• Use AI and advanced analytics, where appropriate and compliant, to identify patterns, test hypotheses, improve decision quality and optimize field and omnichannel performance.

Primary Market Research, Customer Understanding and Responsible Data Use

• Own the primary market research strategy, translating senior leadership questions into a prioritized insights plan with clear decision impact, budget rigor and delivery expectations.
• Apply modern research approaches, including digital listening, behavioral science, agile testing, social and search insights, AI-assisted synthesis and mixed-method research, where appropriate and compliant.
• Hold vendors and internal partners accountable for quality, delivery, compliance with AstraZeneca policies, data privacy and responsible AI principles, while sharing standard processes across teams.

Analytics, Performance Reporting and Digital Transformation

• Orchestrate insights across Brand, Advanced Analytics, Competitive Intelligence, Market Access, Medical, Finance, Digital and other partners to build a coordinated view of performance, opportunity and risk.
• Set direction for benchmark development, dashboards, performance routines and insights storytelling, enabling senior leaders to make timely decisions.
• Lead case analyses, scenario modeling, predictive analytics and opportunity sizing to guide strategic choices.
• Champion scalable ways of working, including automation, self-service analytics, reusable data assets, experimentation and clear governance of AI-enabled tools.

Required Qualifications and Experience

• Bachelor's Degree
• Experience conducting qualitative and quantitative market research across different collaborator groups, including healthcare professionals, patients and payers.
• Five or more years of experience in the pharmaceutical industry.
• Proven ability to conduct analytics using secondary data sources relevant to the pharmaceutical industry, such as IQVIA, Prognos, Decision Resources and patient-level data, as well as experience with performance tracking.
• Strong eye for business, critical-thinking skills and an understanding of sales and marketing practices.
• Ability to influence both laterally and vertically across an organization.
• High emotional intelligence.
• Demonstrated ability to lead projects.
• Ability to manage multiple tasks and assignments to demanding deadlines with minimal supervision.
• Strong interpersonal, collaboration and teamwork skills.
• Comfortable working in a matrix environment.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills.
• Experience leading insights for a specialty product, with knowledge of specialty pharmacy and buy-and-bill distribution and tracking.
• Experience in specialty biologics, respiratory or immunology therapy areas.

Desirable Qualifications and Experience

• A high degree of creativity and innovation in developing new approaches, processes and methodologies.
• Experience conducting pre-product-launch market research, including positioning and segmentation.
• In-depth knowledge of respiratory biologics market dynamics.

Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. In this role, you will serve as a key member of our electrical test engineering team, partnering with engineering, manufacturing, quality, and operations to develop, optimize, and sustain test solutions for sophisticated microwave modules and systems. You will have a direct impact on product quality, yield, cost, and manufacturing efficiency while helping bring innovative new technologies from development into full-scale production.

This position offers a unique opportunity to work with cutting-edge RF and microwave technologies, influence manufacturing strategy, and develop solutions that support mission-critical aerospace and defense applications.

This is a 1st Shift position (Monday through Friday, 8-hour shifts), fully onsite.

Key Responsibilities

• Design, develop, implement, and sustain test methods for complex RF, microwave, and electronic products.
• Develop troubleshooting techniques and diagnostic processes to drive efficient root cause identification and resolution.

• Support New Product Introduction (NPI) activities by ensuring manufacturing readiness, test coverage, and process robustness.
• Analyze product performance, yield data, equipment performance, and manufacturing metrics to identify opportunities for continuous improvement.
• Lead initiatives focused on increasing yield, improving product quality, reducing manufacturing costs, and enhancing operational efficiency.
• Participate in the design, review, and implementation of new test equipment, fixtures, and production tools.
• Drive projects from concept through production launch while meeting quality, cost, and schedule objectives.
• Provide technical leadership, training, and support to technicians and manufacturing personnel.
• Work collaboratively with suppliers, subcontractors, and other ADI/ADFED locations as needed to resolve technical challenges and improve overall product performance.

Qualifications

Required

• U.S. Citizen with the ability and willingness to obtain a security clearance.
• Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering or a related engineering discipline.
• Knowledge of RF, microwave, analog, or mixed-signal electronics.
• Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills.
• Experience interpreting technical data and using data-driven decision-making to solve engineering problems.
• Excellent communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively across cross-functional teams.
• Ability to manage multiple priorities and drive projects to successful completion.

Preferred

• Experience in aerospace, defense, semiconductor, or high-reliability manufacturing environments.

• Hands-on experience with RF test equipment such as network analyzers, spectrum analyzers, power meters, signal generators, and oscilloscopes.

• Experience supporting manufacturing test operations and New Product Introduction (NPI).

• Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement experience.

Preferred Qualifications

jobs.title: Senior Clinical Solutions Engineer, Data - Evinova
jobs.description:
About the Role:

As a Senior Clinical Solutions Engineer, Data, you’ll be the customer-facing clinical data expert on our SaaS Delivery team and a trusted advisor on data requirements, data standards, and technical solutions for connecting with Evinova’s SaaS solutions. You’ll work across clinical trial operational, study design, cost and rate, and feasibility data, leading customer conversations about data requirements and then building and guiding the work that gets customer data into our platform, from source data through validated loads. You’ll also be a domain expert across the product suite, supporting post-implementation technical inquiries and contributing to pre-sales discussions.

You’ll work directly with customers’ clinical operations, data, and IT teams, and with our Product and Engineering teams, to turn customer needs into working solutions. You’ll stay close to products in development and translate their requirements into delivery approaches. Our product space is new, so this role suits someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment, is energized by emerging technology, and is happy to roll up their sleeves to deliver digital health solutions at scale.

What You’ll Do

Lead customer data conversations

• Lead discovery with customers on data requirements, identifying the right datasets, data owners, and multi-functional partners for each data type.

• Advise customers on data standards and on how their data maps to Evinova’s out-of-the-box offerings.

• Develop deep expertise in Evinova’s data landscape and in customer data architectures, providing technical guidance during implementation and configuration.

• Present clearly and confidently to technical and non-technical audiences, including senior customer collaborators.

Technical implementation

• Guide customers through collecting source data specifications, preparing datasets, and mapping and transforming data to Evinova standards where needed.

• Support customer onboarding to ingest sponsor-specific data sources.

• Build and prepare data work hands-on where needed, and load them into customer environments.

• Review customer-provided data for quality and completeness, and resolve issues before load.

• Validate loaded data in customer environments and reconcile it against source.

• Manage defects and issues through to resolution in partnership with Product and Engineering, and lead root-cause analysis and remediation.

• Navigate formal change control and environment promotion, coordinating approvals, dependencies, and timelines.

• Champion change initiatives using change-management guidelines, aligning delivery with strategic goals, product releases, and multi-functional needs during complex transitions.

• Track and communicate implementation progress across customers and internal partners, working independently across multiple engagements and proactively identifying and mitigating risks.

Integrations

• Lead all aspects of end-to-end customer data integration, including collecting requirements, configuring, testing, and maintaining integrations, and fix connectivity issues.

• Manage configuration as code and coordinate reviews and approvals with Platform and Security partners.

• Support system-upgrade impact assessments and update integrations after implementation.

• Ensure data exchange meets applicable data privacy and regulatory requirements

Be the product SME

• Answer post-implementation technical and data questions and serve as a customer concern point for data-related issues.

• Support pre-sales with technical and data questions, such as feasibility and prioritization.

• Act as a key liaison between customers, internal teams, vendors, and our Product and Engineering teams, and work with Product to build solutions and feed customer insights back into the roadmap.

• Establish and document guidelines for data exchange, including monitoring and to fix, and develop and optimize delivery playbooks, templates, and checklists that make use of Evinova’s automated tools.

• Train internal teams and customers on data exchange procedures and standards.

• Keep a commercial approach, making sure integration and delivery work brings value for customers and for Evinova.

Essential Qualifications

• 8+ years of experience
• Bachelor's Degree
• Demonstrated experience in clinical operations, clinical data management, clinical trial planning, or a related technical field where data informs study decisions.

• Strong working knowledge of clinical trial data structures, terminologies, and standards, including USDM and CDISC.

• Hands-on familiarity with clinical trial operational, study design, cost and rate, and feasibility data, ideally including both clinical operational data and cost or finance data.

• Good background in the technical implementation of customer-facing data integrations across organizations, ideally for enterprise SaaS customers.

• Strong working skills with structured data formats and secure file transfer.

• Comfort with configuration in version control, command-line tools, and basic cloud concepts (for example, AWS).

• Experience with work-tracking and documentation tools such as Jira and Confluence.

• Demonstrated ability to analyze data flows, identify discrepancies, and solve complex data issues.

• Ability to manage high-visibility, technical customer engagements, work independently across multiple engagements, and own problems end to end.

• Executive presence and good communication, with the ability to translate technical topics for non-technical audiences and collaborate across diverse teams.

• Highly organized and passionate about finding effective approaches. Shows resilience and adaptability in a fast-paced, newly emerging product space. Has a passion for improving healthcare through technology.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience supporting or implementing healthcare technology, digital health solutions, or data-heavy SaaS platforms.

• Knowledge of data privacy and compliance requirements and standards for clinical data.

• Experience working within formal change management in a regulated environment.

• Experience supporting pre-sales or solution scoping.

• Familiarity with integration monitoring tools, automation, and customer delivery playbooks.

• Practical experience applying AI-driven tools or frameworks to accelerate data integration and validation (for example, reducing manual mapping).

When we put unexpected teams in the same room, we unleash bold thinking with the power to encourage life-changing medicines. But that doesn't mean we're not flexible. We balance the expectation of being in the office while respecting individual flexibility. Join us in our unique and ambitious world.

Why Evinova (AstraZeneca)?

Evinova draws on AstraZeneca’s deep experience developing novel therapeutics, informed by insights from thousands of patients and clinical researchers. Together, we accelerate the delivery of life-changing medicines, improve the design and delivery of clinical trials for better patient experiences and outcomes, and think more holistically about patient care before, during, and after treatment.

Evinova represents an outstanding opportunity to deliver meaningful outcomes with digital and AI to serve the wider healthcare community and create new standards for the sector. We work a minimum of three days per week from the office to maintain the pace, connection, and creative friction that builds great products, while respecting individual flexibility.

Join us on our journey of building a new kind of health tech business to reset expectations of what a biopharmaceutical company can be. This means opening new ways to work, pioneering ground breaking methods, and bringing unexpected teams together. Interested? Come and join our journey.

jobs.title: Engineering Advisor - Integrated Solutions/ Well Engineering
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about well engineering, operational excellence, and delivering innovative energy solutions?

Do you enjoy designing and optimizing well operations, solving complex engineering challenges, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to deliver safe, efficient, and cost-effective projects?

Partnering with the Best

As an Engineering Advisor - Integrated Solutions/ Well Engineering, you will take ownership of delivering well designs, technical requirements, and operational plans to achieve Baker Hughes' and our customers' technical and financial objectives. You will work closely with Service Delivery, HSE, Finance, Commercial, Sales, and other Baker Hughes product lines to ensure successful project planning and execution.

Fueling Your Passion

As an Engineering Advisor - Integrated Solutions/ Well Engineering, you will leverage your technical expertise, operational experience, and problem-solving capabilities to support the planning and execution of Integrated Solutions projects. You will drive engineering excellence, optimize well performance, manage operational risks, and ensure the delivery of safe, efficient, and cost-effective well operations.

As an Engineering Advisor - Integrated Solutions/ Well Engineering, you will be responsible for:

• Ensuring all engineering activities comply with HSE policies and procedures while promoting a strong safety culture and Baker Hughes' Culture Pillars.
• Participating in tender and bid preparation processes by providing technical well engineering input.
• Preparing and reviewing well designs, operational plans, and procedures for well construction, completion, intervention, and abandonment activities.
• Defining technical rig specifications, service requirements, and third-party equipment and service needs.
• Developing and reviewing operational schedules, time estimates, and well cost projections to support project planning and execution.
• Preparing risk registers, contingency plans, and mitigation strategies in collaboration with internal and external stakeholders.
• Leading and participating in technical peer reviews, quality assurance activities, and engineering assessments.
• Monitoring daily operational progress, project expenditure, and technical performance against established objectives and KPIs.
• Providing technical recommendations and engineering support to project teams to optimize well performance and operational efficiency.
• Identifying and implementing best practices, technological advancements, and continuous improvement initiatives across Integrated Solutions operations.
• Collaborating with customers, wellsite personnel, and project stakeholders to ensure effective communication and flawless service delivery.
• Leading and participating in Root Cause Analysis investigations, documenting lessons learned, and implementing corrective actions.
• Preparing and reviewing technical reports, including End of Well Reports, after-action reviews, and operational performance summaries.
• Supporting the development and continuous improvement of engineering policies, procedures, and technical documentation.
• Mentoring and coaching engineering team members while contributing to technical knowledge sharing and global best practices.
• Delivering technical presentations, leading customer meetings, and supporting project strategy discussions.

To be successful in this role, you will:

• Have a bachelor's degree in Petroleum Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline. A master's degree in Petroleum, Oil & Gas, or Well Engineering is preferred.
• Have a minimum of 8 years of relevant experience in well construction, completions, intervention, and/or well optimization.
• Demonstrate strong technical expertise in drill bits and mills, Bottom Hole Assembly (BHA) design, engineering simulations, field operations, and well program preparation.
• Have hands-on experience in Lump Sum Turnkey (LSTK) projects and well engineering.
• Possess previous experience working in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region.
• Demonstrate experience in at least two of the following applications: conventional rotary drilling, horizontal or multilateral wells, pad drilling, unconventional drilling, coiled tubing drilling, underbalanced or managed pressure drilling, or geothermal well design and operations.
• Have previous experience engaging directly with customers and managing technical stakeholder relationships.
• Possess strong knowledge of well control principles and operational safety requirements.
• Demonstrate proficiency in well engineering and design software, including hydraulics, torque and drag, and casing/tubing design applications.
• Have proficiency in Microsoft Office, Power BI, or other analytical and reporting tools.
• Demonstrate excellent analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities.
• Possess excellent written and verbal English communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex technical information effectively.
• Have strong interpersonal skills and the ability to collaborate across functions, cultures, and organizational levels.

Desired Characteristics

• Proven track record of continuous improvement and optimization of well designs and operational performance.
• Knowledge of geomechanics and its application to well design and drilling operations.
• Strong technical leadership and mentoring capabilities.
• Demonstrated ability to analyze and resolve complex engineering and operational challenges.
• Experience leading technical reviews, engineering projects, and cross-functional initiatives.
• Strong planning, organizational, and project management skills.
• Ability to influence stakeholders and establish credibility with customers and senior leadership.
• Commitment to operational excellence, innovation, and continuous professional development.

Work in a Way That Works for You

This role requires close collaboration with customers, project teams, and cross-functional stakeholders to support the planning, design, and execution of Integrated Solutions projects. The position may involve travel to customer locations, operational sites, and other business locations to support technical discussions, project execution, and operational excellence initiatives.

Working for You

• Career development and training opportunities.
• Medical and wellness benefits.
• Financial and retirement programs.
• Additional voluntary benefits.

• Management of comprehensive launch plans and technical deployments for products that establish rollout timelines, marketing strategies, training initiatives and communication channels to promote the launch new products effectively.
• Monitoring of key metrics such as adoption rates, usage patterns, customer satisfaction (including complaints), and revenue generation to assess the product's performance against set goals.

Assistant Vice President Expectations

• To advise and influence decision making, contribute to policy development and take responsibility for operational effectiveness. Collaborate closely with other functions/ business divisions.
• Lead a team performing complex tasks, using well developed professional knowledge and skills to deliver on work that impacts the whole business function. Set objectives and coach employees in pursuit of those objectives, appraisal of performance relative to objectives and determination of reward outcomes
• If the position has leadership responsibilities, People Leaders are expected to demonstrate a clear set of leadership behaviours to create an environment for colleagues to thrive and deliver to a consistently excellent standard. The four LEAD behaviours are: L – Listen and be authentic, E – Energise and inspire, A – Align across the enterprise, D – Develop others.
• OR for an individual contributor, they will lead collaborative assignments and guide team members through structured assignments, identify the need for the inclusion of other areas of specialisation to complete assignments. They will identify new directions for assignments and/ or projects, identifying a combination of cross functional methodologies or practices to meet required outcomes.
• Consult on complex issues; providing advice to People Leaders to support the resolution of escalated issues.
• Identify ways to mitigate risk and developing new policies/procedures in support of the control and governance agenda.
• Take ownership for managing risk and strengthening controls in relation to the work done.
• Perform work that is closely related to that of other areas, which requires understanding of how areas coordinate and contribute to the achievement of the objectives of the organisation sub-function.
• Collaborate with other areas of work, for business aligned support areas to keep up to speed with business activity and the business strategy.
• Engage in complex analysis of data from multiple sources of information, internal and external sources such as procedures and practises (in other areas, teams, companies, etc).to solve problems creatively and effectively.
• Communicate complex information. 'Complex' information could include sensitive information or information that is difficult to communicate because of its content or its audience.
• Influence or convince stakeholders to achieve outcomes.

All colleagues will be expected to demonstrate the Barclays Values of Respect, Integrity, Service, Excellence and Stewardship – our moral compass, helping us do what we believe is right. They will also be expected to demonstrate the Barclays Mindset – to Empower, Challenge and Drive – the operating manual for how we behave.

Are you an experienced Product professional who is passionate about turning customer insight into compelling propositions and better experiences? As an AVP Product and Proposition Manager, you will play a leading role in shaping product and proposition strategy, overseeing performance, identifying opportunities for innovation and guiding delivery from initial concept through to launch and continuous improvement. You will bring together customer feedback, market insight, data and commercial considerations to make informed decisions, navigate complex challenges, and deliver products and journeys that create sustainable value for customers and the business.

To be successful in the role, you must have the following experience:

• End-to-end product ownership experience, including product design and features, product lifecycle, and delivering enhancements to customer experiences.
• Applying a controls-by-design mindset within a risk and controls environment, including experience supporting remediation work.
• Understanding the voice of the customer and translating NPS, complaints and wider customer insight into meaningful decisions and actions.
• Using data and insight to inform product decisions and support go-to-market activity, working collaboratively with research, data, marketing and channel teams.
• Working with AI, machine learning and emerging digital technologies, with an understanding of how innovation can support improved customer and business outcomes.
• Applying considerable analytical, interpretative and commercial skills to complex problems and translating insight into practical solutions.
• Collaborating effectively across diverse teams and communicate clearly with a range of stakeholders.
• Contributing to the future of financial services with a clear focus on improving outcomes for customers and clients.

Some other highly valued experience may include:

• Experience leading product, proposition, and business transformation initiatives within savings and/or insurance.
• Consulting experience, ideally gained within a Big Four strategy consulting firm, with exposure to large-scale transformation programmes and strategic change initiatives.
• Relevant qualifications and professional certifications aligned to the role.
• A recognised accounting qualification.

We will nurture your talent through the FutureXcelerator, a two-year accelerated development opportunity designed for high-potential, future-focused individuals with a passion for technology, data and innovation. Time will be given to you, alongside performing in the role, to gain broad exposure to how a large financial services organisation operates, while building the commercial, strategic and customer-led thinking needed to make a meaningful impact, build a breadth of experience and a good internal network.

You may be assessed on the key critical skills relevant for success in role, such as risk and controls, change and transformation, business acumen strategic thinking and digital and technology, as well as job-specific technical skills.

This role is based in London. Barclays operates a hybrid working model, and colleagues in this role will be expected to attend the office on agreed anchor days in line with the team they join.

jobs.title: Quality SME, Production & Process Controls
jobs.description:
This is where your work makes a difference.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Our Baxter colleagues are united by our Mission to Save and Sustain Lives. Together, our community is driven by a culture of courage, trust, and collaboration. Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

Your Role at Baxter

This is where your creativity addresses challenges

You are creative, thorough, and a heads-down do-er. You embrace a challenge and truly apply the collaborative powers of your team to produce great results. You are motivated by work that is never the same from one day to the next. As a Quality Manager II, you are unafraid of navigating through necessary internal processes to facilitate a product you deeply believe in. You can absorb and act on complex procedures and data and train your team or peers if needed. You take pride in getting things done quickly without sacrificing safety or quality.

Your Team at Baxter

Within Quality, every role makes a difference. Products that Baxter makes are shipped worldwide for patients in need. Whether it's building a new process from scratch or facing a never-before-seen production hurdle, individuals within Quality are given the trust and opportunity to bring creativity to the table. Regardless of your specific role, it is sure to touch a portion of our global operation.

The mission of Baxter is to save and sustain lives. This mission is embedded into everything we do. This means if there is a decision to be made where quantity and quality are at odds, we will always choose quality. Our patients come first, always.

The Quality function values both working together as a team and independently. We draw energy from working in a plant or an office where there are opportunities to collaborate. As the company evolves, so does the way our team approaches work as it strives to create top-of-the-line products.

We build relationships with each other to get work done. Building these relationships is easy because we all share common traits of being reliable, ethical, and caring. We lean on our colleagues for their expertise and hold each other accountable. We feel empowered to speak up when there's a new insight or opportunity to improve something. This open dialog builds trust within the team and helps create a better product for our customers.

What you'll be doing

• Serve as the division Quality Compliance technical SME for production and process controls, including statistical sampling, in-process control checks, manufacturing process flows, and batch record compliance across ITP sites.
• Provide strategic and technical Quality Compliance guidance on production and process controls for sterile preparations, with a focus on manufacturing process controls and their compliance adequacy.
• Provide specialist guidance and independent compliance assessment of visual inspection programs, including inspection methods, qualification, defect classification, acceptance criteria, sampling strategies, investigations, and inspection performance trends.
• Provide specialist Quality Compliance guidance on particulate matter prevention and control, including assessment of particulate sources, monitoring and trending, investigation adequacy, and the effectiveness of site-owned corrective and preventive actions.
• Provide specialist Quality Compliance guidance on container closure integrity testing (CCIT), including review of testing strategies, method suitability and validation, lifecycle controls, investigations, and remediation adequacy, in partnership with relevant site functions and the Sterility Assurance SME.
• Support all sites in sustaining an Always Inspection Ready state through risk-based assessments, readiness reviews, mock inspections, coaching, and timely closure of identified gaps.
• Provide direct technical support during health authority inspections, including real-time assessment of production and process control questions, evidence review, response development, and follow-up commitments.
• Lead or support technical compliance assessments and remediation oversight associated with inspection observations, regulatory commitments, significant quality signals, and systemic production or process control weaknesses; challenge whether site-owned actions are risk-based, sustainable, and verified for effectiveness.
• Independently assess end-to-end manufacturing processes for compliance with approved procedures, validated process requirements, product specifications, and regulatory expectations, and recommend actions to address identified gaps.

• Perform and lead risk-based assessments of manufacturing operations, process control systems, production practices, manufacturing documentation, and operational execution.
• Review and challenge manufacturing-related deviations, investigations, process excursions, batch failures, human error events, repeat deviations, and product impact assessments.
• Evaluate process control strategies, in-process monitoring programs, alarm management practices, and manufacturing controls to ensure consistent product quality and process robustness.

• Provide technical compliance guidance on site-owned remediation plans addressing manufacturing compliance gaps, process weaknesses, recurring deviations, and inspection observations; review their adequacy and effectiveness.
• Assess procedural adherence, manufacturing discipline, shift execution, line clearance practices, batch documentation practices, and operational GMP behaviors; identify compliance gaps and recommend improvements to accountable site functions.
• Provide independent compliance review and technical guidance on proposed manufacturing process changes and standardization, using quality risk management and process performance monitoring to assess whether controls remain adequate.

• Partner with site leadership to improve investigation quality, root cause analysis, CAPA effectiveness, and operational ownership of compliance issues.
• Conduct site assessments, manufacturing system reviews, gap analyses, and mock inspections to identify vulnerabilities and opportunities for improvement.
• Monitor manufacturing compliance performance, recurring trends, process capability indicators, and operational risk signals, escalating significant concerns as necessary.
• Coach and mentor manufacturing, quality, and technical personnel on production controls, process discipline, GMP expectations, and regulatory requirements.

• Interpret current regulatory expectations and industry best practices related to pharmaceutical manufacturing operations and process control systems, and advise site functions on compliant implementation.

What you'll bring

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Pharmacy, Chemistry, Life Sciences, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, or related technical discipline required.
• Advanced degree preferred.

• Minimum 15 years of experience in pharmaceutical quality, compliance, manufacturing, process engineering, technical services, or related technical functions, including substantial experience assessing production and process controls from a quality and compliance perspective.

• Experience in sterile manufacturing, injectable products, IV solutions, aseptic processing, biologics, or combination products.

Position Summary

BMS Cruiserath Biologics is seeking to recruit one permanent Engineering CQV, Sr. Specialist – Cleaning Validation. The role is part of the Engineering Commissioning, Qualification and Validation (CQV) team and will support Cleaning Validation activities across the Multi-Product Cell Culture (MPCC) and Sterile Drug Product Facility (SDPF) sites. The successful candidate will report to the Sr. Manager, Engineering CQV.

The role will provide technical leadership and subject matter expertise for the development, execution, and lifecycle management of cleaning validation programmes for manufacturing equipment. The position will ensure cleaning processes are scientifically justified, compliant with applicable regulatory expectations, and maintained in a validated state.

Key Responsibilities

•  Operate as part of the Engineering CQV team under a campus approach, supporting Cleaning Validation activities across the MPCC and SDPF facilities.

•  Define scientifically justified cleaning acceptance criteria using health-based exposure limits and applicable product, process, and equipment data.

•  Perform and document worst-case product and equipment assessments, including equipment grouping, bracketing, and matrixing strategies where appropriate.

•  Develop sampling plans for swab and rinse samples, including selection and justification of sampling locations, methods, and recovery studies.

•  Provide Cleaning Validation input to user requirements, design reviews, commissioning and qualification plans, equipment modifications, and start-up activities.

•  Assess changes, deviations, cleaning failures, process modifications, and new product introductions for potential impact on the validated state.

•  Support investigations, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, and implementation of effective remediation plans.

•  Ensure Cleaning Validation documentation is technically accurate, complete, current, traceable, and audit-ready.

•  Support continued process verification, periodic review, monitoring, and lifecycle management of the Cleaning Validation programme.

•  Identify and implement opportunities for process improvement, standardisation, digital enablement, and enhanced compliance.

•  Communicate plans, progress, risks, and results clearly to key stakeholders and governance forums.

•  Provide training, coaching, and technical support to team members on Cleaning Validation principles, procedures, and regulatory expectations.

•  Demonstrated experience in Cleaning Validation within a pharmaceutical, biopharmaceutical, or other regulated manufacturing environment.

•  Strong knowledge of Cleaning Validation principles, including health-based exposure limits, maximum allowable carryover calculations, worst-case selection, equipment grouping, sampling strategies, and cleaning process lifecycle management.

•  Knowledge of applicable regulatory requirements and industry guidance, including FDA and EMA expectations, ICH Q7 and ICH Q9, and ASTM E3106.

•  Experience authoring and executing Cleaning Validation plans, protocols, reports, risk assessments, and technical justifications.

•  Experience assessing deviations, changes, and investigation outcomes for impact on the validated state.

This role is responsible for leading all commissioning, qualification (IQ, OQ, PQ), and requalification activities for critical facility and process utilities across the MPCC and SDPF facilities, including WFI and purified water systems, clean steam, compressed air and process gases, CIP/SIP skids, HVAC systems and cleanrooms, and Building/Environmental Monitoring Systems (BMS/EMS). Bristol Myers Squibb is seeking a Senior Scientist to join the Oral Product Development group within the Drug Product Development function. The drug product development group supports the formulation and process development of Bristol Myers Squibb’s drug candidates from preclinical stage to commercial process readiness.  This position is responsible for formulation design, development, characterization, and technology transfer to enable development of small molecule drug products (DPs). The incumbent will be accountable as an individual contributor to support formulation development as well as providing necessary guidance and support of drug product control strategy for drug candidates across all stages of development.

The Senior Scientist will collaborate across BMS sites with Drug Product, Analytical, API, Quality, and Regulatory functions to execute drug product formulation/process development, formulation strategies, control strategies, and support of drug application submissions and approval.

Shaping the Future of Clinical Science

At Bristol Myers Squibb, we are united by a single purpose: transforming patients' lives through science. Our Global Drug Development team sits at the heart of that mission, and we are now looking for an outstanding Associate Director, Global Clinical Scientist to join us.

This is a role for someone who thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment, who takes pride in scientific rigour, and who wants to see their expertise translated directly into clinical programmes that matter.

What You Will Be Part Of

As a member of our clinical development team, you will take on meaningful ownership of one or more clinical trials, leading their design, implementation, and execution from start-up through to close-out. Working alongside Global Development Operations protocol managers, Medical Monitors, Clinical Indication Leads, and cross-functional colleagues, you will help drive studies forward with precision and purpose.

This is not a siloed role. You will provide scientific and clinical leadership to supporting Clinical Scientists, co-lead study team meetings, and serve as a primary liaison with external partners. You will also contribute to future clinical development planning, ensuring our programmes are built on the strongest possible scientific foundation.

What You Will Do

• Lead the planning and execution of all study activities across multiple trials, with a high degree of autonomy
• Maintain deep protocol expertise and act as the clinical knowledge hub for your study team
• Collaborate on protocol and Informed Consent Form (ICF) development, including writing, reviewing, and resolution of cross-functional comments
• Oversee data generation and validation activities, including CRF design, clinical data review, and query resolution
• Identify clinical data trends and escalate observations appropriately to the Medical Monitor
• Develop clinical narrative plans and review clinical narratives
• Support site-facing activities, including training and serving as the primary contact for clinical questions
• Contribute to the drafting, review, and validation of Clinical Study Reports (CSRs) and regulatory documents such as Investigators' Brochures, DSURs, and regulatory responses
• Evaluate innovative trial designs in collaboration with the Medical Monitor and Clinical Indication Lead
• Support study committee activities, including Data Monitoring Committees

What You Will Bring

Education A degree in Life Sciences is required. MD, PhD, PharmD, MS, RN, or equivalent scientific qualifications are preferred.

Experience

• 5 or more years of experience in clinical science, clinical research, or an equivalent field
• Proficient knowledge of GCP/ICH guidelines, drug development processes, study design, and statistics
• Skilled in programme-specific data review, trend identification, and data interpretation
• Familiarity with the establishment and operation of data monitoring committees, dose review teams, and independent response adjudication committees

Competencies

• Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills with the ability to engage effectively across functions and seniority levels
• A collaborative mindset with proven ability to lead team activities and matrix-based groups
• Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills with a commitment to quality and detail
• Proficient in medical terminology and medical writing
• Deep understanding of relevant disease areas, compounds, mechanisms of action, PK/PD, and biomarker and safety profiles
• Skilled in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, plus electronic data capture tools such as RAVE and J-Review
• Adaptable and composed under pressure, able to manage shifting priorities with confidence and professionalism

jobs.description:
At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it.

The Opportunity

Field teams are where strategy meets reality. They are the vital link between innovative medicines and the healthcare professionals and patients who depend on them — and making sure those teams are equipped, focused, and firing at their best is one of the most consequential things a commercial organisation can get right.

This is that role.

As Field Force Excellence Lead for the Northern Cluster, you will set the standard for how BMS field teams plan, prioritise, and execute across the UK, Ireland, and the Nordics. You will own the frameworks, build the capabilities, and drive the data-led engagement practices that determine how effectively our medicines reach the patients who need them.

This is a rare opportunity to leave a defining mark on the capability and culture of a world-class commercial organisation — and on the patients whose lives we are working to transform.

What You Will Be Doing

Field Excellence Strategy and Governance

You will serve as the strategic lead for field excellence across UK&IE — bringing clarity, consistency, and genuine ambition to how teams perform. That means owning and embedding the KAM and Field Excellence Playbook, co-leading the definition of customer engagement KPIs, and reporting performance insights to leadership. You will analyse what is working, identify what is not, and work with field leaders, Medical, and Market Access to drive continuous improvement across the full asset lifecycle.

Capability Building and Training

You will partner with Brand teams and global training functions to assess and elevate field team capabilities — identifying gaps, designing targeted development interventions, and championing a culture of continuous learning. Whether it is clinical knowledge, customer engagement skills, or pipeline readiness, you will make sure the team has what it needs to perform.

Key Account Management

You will own the end-to-end KAM process, ensuring the 3M model — Marketing, Medical, Market Access — is applied with the right level of focus at each stage of the asset lifecycle. You will lead the Strategic Account Management approach, develop the strategy for external data acquisition, and simplify the handoff moments between teams so that account knowledge and relationships never fall through the cracks.

Engagement Capabilities and Commercialisation Operations

You will lead the local adoption of new engagement capabilities, provide oversight of commercialisation operations — tools, incentive schemes, resourcing structures — and partner with Launch Excellence and New Product Planning leads to make sure field readiness is built early and systematically ahead of every key launch milestone.

Cross-Functional and Global Collaboration

You will build strong working relationships with global, cluster, and local stakeholders, acting as a credible and influential voice for UK&IE at a European and global level. You will shape how global frameworks land locally — making sure they are adapted, not just adopted.

What We Are Looking For

Essential

• Strong experience in a relevant pharmaceutical or healthcare role, with demonstrated expertise in field excellence, commercial operations, or customer engagement strategy
• Proven track record building and executing field excellence frameworks in a complex, matrixed environment
• Strong working knowledge of the UK&IE healthcare landscape, including hospital structures, customer networks, and market access dynamics
• Deep understanding of field force reporting, targeting, cycle planning, and territory design in a multi-country context
• Proven experience in Key Account Management and account-based engagement models
• Comfortable working with customer-level data and advanced analytical techniques to drive channel strategy
• Demonstrated ability to lead technical implementations — new tools, systems, and platforms — end-to-end
• Bachelor's degree in Business, Life Sciences, Marketing, Data Analytics, or a related field; postgraduate qualification preferred
• Excellent written and spoken English; a Nordic language is an advantage

Preferred

• Experience in oncology, haematology, or immunology, with an understanding of the specialist customer landscape
• Prior experience in a field-based commercial role such as Key Account Manager or Medical Sales Specialist
• Familiarity with Veeva CRM and other field-facing digital tools
• Experience working in a cluster or multi-market structure with cross-border collaboration
• Knowledge of incentive compensation design and field force sizing methodologies
• Experience in launch excellence or new product planning
• Exposure to European Markets or global pharmaceutical functions
• Hands-on experience building analytics and reporting solutions, such as Power BI dashboards

What Makes Someone Successful Here

You think strategically but you are not precious about getting into the detail. You are equally comfortable presenting to senior leadership and working through a data set with a field manager. You lead through influence rather than authority, you make decisions with confidence under ambiguity, and you are genuinely energised by building something — not just maintaining it.

You will be working across Oncology, Cardiovascular, and CAR-T/Haematology therapy areas, partnering with Sales, Medical, Market Access, and Commercial Operations teams across multiple markets and legal entities. It is a broad, complex, high-visibility role — and for the right person, that is exactly the point.

As Value Creation Manager at BMS, you will be the strategic architect of wraparound value across the UK&IE portfolio — owning and forging partnerships with compounders, Patient Support Programme delivery organisations, private market stakeholders, and NHS customers to unlock real, measurable value for patients and the business.

This is not a traditional commercial role. It sits at the intersection of brand strategy, market access, and external partnerships — and it demands someone who is bold enough to identify opportunities others haven't seen yet, and capable enough to execute on them.

If you are commercially sharp, relationship-driven, and genuinely energised by complexity — read on.

What You Will Be Doing

Portfolio Value Strategy You will partner with Brand teams to own and execute a comprehensive Value Creation Plan that maximises the commercial and patient value of the BMS UK&IE portfolio. That means proactively identifying and pursuing high-potential opportunities across compounders, PSP delivery organisations, and the private market — and serving as the strategic lead for all commercial partnership organisations.

Patient Support Programmes and Collaborative Working You will act as process owner for the end-to-end set-up and management of Joint Working agreements and PSP programmes, working closely with Brand, Procurement, and administrative teams to ensure governance is robust and delivery is seamless. Compliance and value creation are not in tension here — you will make sure they go hand in hand.

Private Market and Strategic Partnerships Working alongside Market Access and Brand teams, you will build and develop relationships within the private healthcare market, establishing commercial partnership agreements and leading the identification of distribution opportunities for late-stage portfolio assets.

NHS Customer Network You will build a targeted network of NHS ICB customers to monitor the entry of locally commissioned assets — making sure BMS is optimally positioned from commissioning through launch and into lifecycle. You will also develop an influential network of NHS pharmacy leads and network managers to drive uptake and proactively manage loss of exclusivity scenarios.

Compounder Management You will manage and grow strategic relationships with compounders, acting as the primary BMS point of contact and identifying opportunities to optimise both top-line revenue and bottom-line performance.

Essential

• Proven ability to operate in a highly matrixed environment, leading and influencing without direct authority
• Strong knowledge of the UK healthcare landscape — NHS structures, ICBs, commissioning pathways, and the private market
• A proactive, solutions-oriented mindset: someone who spots opportunities early, makes confident decisions, and drives execution at pace

Preferred

• Experience with Patient Support Programmes, Joint Working frameworks, or collaborative working arrangements within pharma
• Familiarity with compounder relationships or specialist distribution models in the UK
• Exposure to late-stage portfolio strategy or LOE planning
• Experience working with Market Access teams on private market or access strategy

This role will suit someone who is as comfortable building relationships as they are building a business case. At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it.

The Associate Director, U.S. Commercial Sales & GTN Analysis position provides strategic support to the U.S. business (with a multi-billion gross to net adjustments “GTN” and net sales, the largest BMS Commercial unit) by leading the close and projection pillars of GTN Finance. This role manages the monthly/quarterly accounting close, account reconciliations, and forward-looking gross-to-net projections across the U.S. product portfolio (Oncology, Immunology & Cardiovascular, Neuroscience, CAR-T & Established Brands).

The Associate Director owns the integrity of the GTN close (accrual sheets, B/S reconciliations, SOX controls) and the projection/variance analysis that leadership relies on to understand gross-to-net drivers. While close and projections are the primary focus, this role will strategically partner and support Innovation initiatives (e.g., Anaplan, PowerBI dashboarding, process automation) where its close/projection subject-matter expertise can accelerate adoption.

This role is highly visible and partners closely with U.S. Brand Finance, Market Access & Pricing, Corporate Accounting, Business Controls, Commercialization AI Strategy & Analytics (“CASA”), external auditors, and the Anaplan systems teams. It provides significant development in financial analysis, commercial model exposure, internal controls, and cross-matrix leadership.

Major Responsibilities and Accountabilities:

• Prepare/create budget/projection timelines, presentations, and sales analysis to effectively communicate strategic insights and drivers of gross-net-variances in partnership with Market Access & Pricing, CASA and US Brand Finance teams.
• Manage the monthly/quarterly gross-to-net close process, including accrual sheets for the major gross-to-net components (e.g., rebates, chargebacks, coupons, discount programs, etc.), government payment allocations, and account reconciliations, validating adequacy of accrual balances.
• Lead GTN variance analysis, drivers & commentary, and presentation materials that communicate gross-to-net insights to finance leadership across the organization.
• Maintain and update the internal control environment for gross-to-net, supporting internal/external audits and the annual SOX compliance process in partnership with Business Controls.
• Partner with Market Access & Pricing on government/regulatory pricing calculations and related entries (e.g., federal and state pricing programs, government pricing adjustments) and monitor regulatory changes affecting gross-to-net.
• Lead net price and price/volume analysis, returns review, and discount/rebate projection reviews to support quarterly close and forecasting.
• Support brand finance pipeline reviews, driver tie-outs, and the reporting dataset used for GTN reporting.
• Flex into Innovation-pillar initiatives (platform enhancements, dashboard build-outs, process automation testing) leveraging close/projection expertise to inform tool design and validate outputs.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

• Minimum education of a bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, economics, information systems, or related field is required. CPA or Master of accounting preferred.
• Minimum of seven (7) years of professional experience within finance, accounting, information systems, or related field is required.
• Solid accounting understanding is a must, with a general understanding of the Pharma industry and U.S. healthcare system.
• Strong analytical skills; ability to work effectively across a matrix organization and influence others at all levels.
• Working knowledge of SAP, Power BI, Hyperion, and Anaplan; strong Excel proficiency.
• Experience with SOX controls and external audit support preferred.

#LI-Hybrid

We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway.

Princeton - NJ - US: $155,640 - $188,593
